questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly distinguishes xylem from phloem? #490

options.a: Both xylem and phloem transport only water
options.b: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to leaves; phloem transports organic food (sucrose) from leaves to other parts
options.c: Both xylem and phloem transport only food
options.d: Phloem transports water; xylem transports food

questions.explanation: Xylem: vascular tissue that transports water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves (one-way flow, transpiration-driven). Phloem: vascular tissue that transports organic food (mainly sucrose) from leaves to other parts of the plant (two-way, translocation).

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the result of meiosis? #491

options.a: Meiosis produces four genetically different haploid daughter cells from one diploid parent cell
options.b: Meiosis produces two identical diploid daughter cells
options.c: Meiosis is a type of asexual reproduction
options.d: Meiosis produces only one daughter cell

questions.explanation: Meiosis: a single diploid parent cell undergoes two divisions (Meiosis I and II) to produce four genetically different haploid (n) gametes. This introduces genetic variation via crossing-over and independent assortment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the structure of the plasma membrane? #492

options.a: A single layer of proteins with no lipids
options.b: A phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins (fluid mosaic model)
options.c: A rigid solid layer of cellulose

questions.explanation: The plasma membrane has a fluid mosaic structure: a phospholipid bilayer with various proteins embedded, giving it selective permeability and flexibility.

questions.questionText: What happens during the Prophase stage of mitosis? #493

options.a: Chromosomes align at the cell equator
options.b: Chromosomes condense and become visible; nuclear membrane disintegrates

questions.explanation: Prophase: Chromosomes condense and become visible; nuclear membrane disintegrates. The order is interphase -> prophase -> metaphase -> anaphase -> telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

questions.questionText: What happens during the Metaphase stage of mitosis? #494

options.a: Chromosomes align at the cell equator
options.c: Chromosomes align at the cell equator (metaphase plate)

questions.explanation: Metaphase: Chromosomes align at the cell equator (metaphase plate). The order is interphase -> prophase -> metaphase -> anaphase -> telophase, followed by cytokinesis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct equation for aerobic respiration? #495

options.d: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy (ATP)

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + ATP (energy). Occurs in mitochondria in the presence of oxygen.

questions.questionText: In human muscle cells during vigorous exercise, anaerobic respiration produces: #496

options.c: Glucose -> Lactic Acid + small amount of Energy (in animal muscle cells during intense exercise)

questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in animals (muscle): glucose -> lactic acid + small amount of ATP (energy). In plants/yeast: glucose -> ethanol + CO2 + small ATP (alcoholic fermentation).

questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes human gamete production and fertilisation? #499

options.a: Both gametes are produced in the liver
options.c: Gametes are produced in the stomach
options.d: Male gametes (sperm) are produced in the testis; female gametes (ova) are produced in the ovary. Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct (fallopian tube) to form a zygote

questions.explanation: Male gametes (sperm) are produced by spermatogenesis in the testes (testis). Female gametes (ova/eggs) are produced by oogenesis in the ovaries. Fertilisation typically occurs in the oviduct/fallopian tube, where sperm meets egg to form a zygote.
